text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure readings consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg are considered high blood pressure, or hypertension.

Blood pressure is measured using two numbers: systolic (the top number, measuring pressure when the heart beats) and diastolic (the bottom number, measuring pressure when the heart rests between beats). According to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the ranges are:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Elevated: Systolic between 120 and 129, and diastolic less than 80
Stage 1 Hypertension: Systolic between 130 and 139, or diastolic between 80 and 89
Stage 2 Hypertension: Systolic of 140 or higher, or diastolic of 90 or higher

text_blocks.snippet: A reading higher than 180/120 mm Hg is an emergency called a hypertensive crisis. If you get this reading, wait a few minutes and test again. If it remains this high, or if you have symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, or vision changes, seek medical care right away.
